topics: 🔁 Lost Your Place? — where to return when you err in Shema and cannot remember where; Rabbi Yoḥanan's rule
🌳 Shema Up a Tree — laborers may recite atop a tree or a wall, but may not pray there; the olive and fig exception
🎯 Intent While Working — Rav Sheshet: idle for the first paragraph, work through the second
🍞 The Laborer's Prayer — full Amida or an abridged one; Grace after Meals cut to two blessings
💍 The Groom's Exemption — 'when you walk along the way', a virgin versus a widow, and why a mourner is different

overview.title: 📖 Overview: Shema in the Tree, Shema at the Wedding
overview.subtitle: Berakhot 16a–16b
overview.hebrewSource: אֵינִי שׁוֹמֵעַ לָכֶם לְבַטֵּל הֵימֶנִי מַלְכוּת שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ שָׁעָה אַחַת
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: After a last word on tents of Torah and streams, the Gemara finishes the previous mishna with a practical Tosefta: what to do when you err in Shema and cannot remember where. Then a new mishna moves from precision to concentration. Laborers may recite Shema perched on a tree or a wall, though they may not pray there, and a groom is exempt from Shema on his wedding night — yet Rabban Gamliel recited it anyway. The Gemara probes how much intent Shema needs, how a laborer's prayer and Grace after Meals are shortened, and why a groom's preoccupation exempts him while a mourner's does not. A second mishna records Rabban Gamliel bathing on the night his wife died and accepting condolences for his slave Tavi, leading to the laws of mourning for slaves. The daf ends with the personal prayers the Sages added after their Amida.

callout.label: The story:
callout.text: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi were tying the wedding canopy for Rabbi Elazar. He slipped off to the study hall, heard this Tosefta being recited before Rabbi Yoḥanan, and came back to teach it to them. They said: had we come only to hear this, it would have been enough for us.

slides.title: 🌳 What May a Laborer Do Without Climbing Down?
slides.subtitle: The mishna and its Tosefta on workers atop trees and walls
rows: Reciting Shema atop a tree or a course of stones
Shema needs less concentration than the Amida
Praying the Amida atop a tree
Only atop an olive or fig tree; on all other trees, climb down
Those trees have dense branches, so one can stand and focus
The homeowner (self-employed) praying atop any tree
His mind is not settled, and it is his prerogative to descend
Idle from work for the first paragraph; Beit Hillel's 'work and recite' is the second paragraph
'Hear, Israel' is compared to 'Pay attention, and hear, Israel' (Deut. 27:9)
Leading the prayer or the Priestly Blessing
So as not to neglect the work they were hired for

callout.label: Prayer and Grace shortened:
callout.text: One baraita has laborers pray the full Amida, another an abridged one. Rav Sheshet first split them between Rabban Gamliel and Rabbi Yehoshua, but since Rabbi Yehoshua permits everyone to abridge, the Gemara concludes both follow Rabban Gamliel: workers paid a wage abridge, workers who work only for their meal pray in full. Similarly, wage-laborers skip the blessing before bread and say two Grace blessings, folding 'Who builds Jerusalem' into the blessing of the land — unless the homeowner reclines with them.

slides.title: 💍 Why Is the Groom Exempt but the Mourner Obligated?
slides.subtitle: The Gemara derives the exemption and then tests its limits

lines.speaker: Baraita
lines.text: 'When you sit in your home' excludes one engaged in a mitzva; 'when you walk along the way' excludes a groom. Hence: one who marries a virgin is exempt, one who marries a widow is obligated.

lines.speaker: Rav Pappa
lines.text: How is it derived? 'Like the way' — just as a journey is voluntary, so all who are obligated are engaged in voluntary matters.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: But surely the verse also covers one walking to perform a mitzva, and still the Torah says: recite!

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: Then it should say 'when walking'. Why בְּלֶכְתְּךָ, 'when you walk'? On your walking you are obligated; on a mitzva's walking you are exempt.

lines.speaker: Gemara
lines.text: Then why only a virgin? Marrying a widow is a mitzva too! — Here he is preoccupied; there he is not. But if preoccupation exempts, one whose ship sank at sea should be exempt too — yet Rav says a mourner is obligated in every mitzva except tefillin, called 'splendor' (Ezekiel 24:17).

lines.speaker: Answer
lines.text: There it is preoccupation with a voluntary matter; here it is preoccupation with a mitzva.

callout.label: May he recite anyway?
callout.text: The mishna says a groom who wishes to recite Shema the first night may. Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: not everyone who wishes to assume the name of piety may assume it.

slides.title: 🛁 Rabban Gamliel Breaks His Own Rules — Three Times
slides.subtitle: Each time his students object, and each time he explains why he is the exception

boxes.title: Shema on his wedding night
items: Students: didn't you teach us a groom is exempt?
'I will not listen to you and remove the Kingdom of Heaven from myself even for one hour'

boxes.title: Bathing the night his wife died
items: Students: didn't you teach us a mourner may not bathe?
'I am not like other people — I am delicate (istenis)'
Gemara: acute mourning at night is only rabbinic — 'the end will be like a bitter day' (Amos 8:10) — and the Sages did not decree it for a delicate person

boxes.title: Condolences for his slave Tavi
items: Students: didn't you teach us one does not accept condolences for slaves?
'Tavi my slave is not like other slaves — he was virtuous'
Baraita: for slaves no row of comforters, no mourners' blessing; Rabbi Yosei allows for a virtuous slave: 'Alas, a good and loyal man who enjoyed his labor'

callout.label: Rabbi Eliezer's maidservant:
callout.text: When students followed him from the upper floor to the gatehouse to the banquet hall to console him, he said: you are not burned even by boiling water! For a slave one says only what one says for an ox or donkey: 'May the Omnipresent replenish your loss.' Likewise only three are called Patriarchs and four Matriarchs, and slaves are not called 'Father so-and-so' — except Rabban Gamliel's, who were significant.

slides.title: 🙏 What the Sages Said After Their Amida
slides.subtitle: Rabbi Elazar's reading of Psalms 63 and the personal prayers that follow

steps.content: 1️⃣ Rabbi Elazar: 'So I will bless You as I live' (Psalms 63:5) is Shema; 'to Your name I will raise my hands' is the Amida. One who does both is satisfied 'as with fat and marrow' and inherits two worlds — 'lips of joys', plural
2️⃣ Rabbi Elazar: may love, brotherhood, peace and friendship dwell in our lot; enlarge our borders with disciples; give us a good companion and a good inclination
3️⃣ Rabbi Yoḥanan: look upon our shame, clothe Yourself in Your mercy, wrap Yourself in Your loving-kindness, and let Your goodness and humility come before You
4️⃣ Rabbi Zeira: that we not sin, nor be ashamed, nor be disgraced before our forefathers. Rabbi Ḥiyya: that Your Torah be our vocation, and our heart not faint nor our eyes dim
5️⃣ Rav: long life — of peace, goodness, blessing, sustenance, vigor, fear of sin, no shame, wealth and honor, love of Torah and fear of Heaven

6️⃣ Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi: save us from the arrogant, from a bad man, a bad mishap, an evil inclination, a bad companion, a bad neighbor, the destructive Satan, a harsh trial and a harsh opponent — even though royal guards stood watch over him

callout.label: Pattern:
callout.text: Each sage's prayer reflects his own concern — disciples, humility, Torah as a livelihood, a long good life, protection from enemies — showing that fixed prayer leaves room for the personal.

summary.principle: Shema demands attention but bends to circumstance: a laborer may recite it in a tree, a groom preoccupied with a mitzva is exempt, yet Rabban Gamliel would not give up the Kingdom of Heaven for even one hour.

flowSteps.content: 🔁 Erred and don't know where → back to the start of the paragraph, the first break, or the first 'writing'; past 'lengthen your days', continue
🌳 Laborers recite Shema atop a tree or wall (idle for the first paragraph); pray only on an olive or fig; wage-laborers abridge the Amida and Grace
❓ Groom exempt: 'when you walk' — voluntary walking, not a mitzva. Widow's groom is not preoccupied; a mourner's preoccupation is voluntary

columns.content: 🛁 Rabban Gamliel: recited Shema as a groom, bathed as a delicate mourner, accepted condolences for virtuous Tavi
🙏 After the Amida each sage added his own prayer — Rabbi Elazar, Rabbi Yoḥanan, Rabbi Zeira, Rabbi Ḥiyya, Rav, Rabbi

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: One engaged in a mitzva is exempt from Shema — but preoccupation alone, like a mourner's, does not exempt

quiz.q: One recited Shema, erred, and does not know where — but realizes it in the middle of a paragraph. According to the Tosefta, what does he do?
o: Returns to the beginning of the entire Shema
Returns to the beginning of that paragraph
Continues from where he is
Returns to 'and you shall write them'
quiz.e: The Tosefta recited before Rabbi Yoḥanan rules: in the middle of a paragraph, return to the beginning of that paragraph; between paragraphs, to the first break; between 'writing' and 'writing', to the first 'writing'. Rabbi Yoḥanan added that once one has begun 'in order to lengthen your days' he simply continues.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara reconcile Rav Sheshet's rule that laborers recite Shema only when idle from work with Beit Hillel's statement that laborers work and recite?
o: Rav Sheshet follows Beit Shammai
Idle from work for the first paragraph; working is permitted during the second paragraph
Idle when atop a tree, working when on the ground
Beit Hillel refer to the homeowner, not to laborers
quiz.e: The Gemara answers: this (idle) refers to the first paragraph of Shema, which requires intent, while that (working) refers to the second paragraph.

quiz.q: Why is one who marries a widow obligated in Shema on his wedding night, even though marrying is also a mitzva?
o: Marrying a widow is not considered a mitzva
He is not preoccupied, whereas one marrying a virgin is
A widow's marriage takes place on a different night
The exemption is only for a Torah scholar
quiz.e: The Gemara explains the distinction as one of preoccupation: 'here he is preoccupied, there he is not.' Only preoccupation with a mitzva, such as a groom's, exempts.

quiz.q: The Gemara asks: if preoccupation exempts a groom, why is a mourner obligated in all mitzvot (except tefillin)? What is its answer?
o: A mourner is in fact exempt from Shema
A mourner's preoccupation is with a voluntary matter; a groom's preoccupation is with a mitzva
A mourner has already accepted the Kingdom of Heaven
Mourning at night is only rabbinic
quiz.e: Rabbi Abba bar Zavda cited Rav that a mourner is obligated in all mitzvot except tefillin, called 'splendor' (Ezekiel 24:17). The Gemara distinguishes: there the preoccupation is voluntary; here, for a groom, it is preoccupation with a mitzva.

quiz.q: How does the Gemara explain Rabban Gamliel bathing on the first night after his wife died?
o: Bathing was permitted for anyone in acute mourning at night
Acute mourning at night is only rabbinic, and the Sages did not decree it for a delicate person (istenis)
His wife's death occurred on a festival, which cancels mourning
He held that a mourner is only prohibited from bathing in hot water
quiz.e: Rabban Gamliel called himself an istenis, a delicate person. The Gemara explains he held that aninut at night is only rabbinic — 'the end will be like a bitter day' (Amos 8:10) — and the Sages did not extend the decree to a delicate person.
